title: Amid El Niño, calamity fund hiked to P45.6B in proposed 2027 budget
summary: The government has proposed an increase in the calamity fund to P45.6 billion under the proposed P7.2 trillion national expenditure program (NEP) for 2027.

blocks.text: The government has proposed an increase in the calamity fund to P45.6 billion under the proposed P7.2 trillion national expenditure program (NEP) for 2027.
According to a report in Balitanghali, the calamity fund rose from the initial P39.8 billion to help the government prepare and recover from the effects of El Niño.
House Minority Leader Marcelino Libanan said that over 80 provinces and cities are expected to be affected by El Niño, citing PAGASA's outlook.
The lawmaker urged government agencies to help in immediately addressing the effects of the weather disturbance.
The El Niño phenomenon is expected to persist until the first half of 2027 and is forecast to be record-breaking in terms of heat, said PAGASA.
The state weather bureau said the prolonged dry spell will lead to drought, and there will be warmer surface temperatures nationwide. –Vince Angelo Ferreras/NB, GMA News
